title: A Stochastic Decision Support System for Cultured Meat Investment: Multi-Criteria Screening, Regulatory Gating and Stage-Gate Monte Carlo Valuation
content: Investors in cultured meat face technical, regulatory and market uncertainties that compound across development stages, while the evidence they rely on is largely modelled, small-scale or company reported. We present CM-IDSS, a stand-alone decision support system that combines stochastic multicriteria screening (SMAA-2) of nine investment archetypes, a stochastic techno-economic cost trajectory, correlated jurisdictional approval gating and stage-gate Monte Carlo valuation with global sensitivity analysis. Inputs were parameterized from a preliminary review of the literature published between 2000 and 2026 and tagged by provenance. In a baseline analysis (20,000 draws, 12% discount rate), no archetype had a positive expected net present value (NPV): values ranged from USD −93 million (whole-cut producer) to −5 million (media and growth-factor supply). Media and growth-factor supply and analytics and quality assurance held the top two screening ranks under four investor profiles, and the whole-cut producer ranked last under all of them. Continuing after technical proof destroyed value for eight of nine archetypes. Expected NPV turned positive only if the 2032 market was 1.2 to 15.6 times the forecast range, depending on archetype, or if technology followed an optimistic trajectory. Rankings were stable in 15 of 17 parameter perturbations but inverted when optimistic technology and a fourfold larger market were combined. The model is a transparent framework for expert calibration, not a forecast.
